chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, and Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:
Ali bin al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who performs what Allah has imposed upon him, he is from the best of the people.'
ai.seo_question: What makes a person one of the best of people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of prominent Kufan narrators like Abu Hamza al-Thumali, this hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) underscores that true superiority in the eyes of God is rooted in the consistent practice of obligatory acts (fara'id). In Shia scholarship, this is often contrasted with mere ritualism, highlighting that the foundation of spiritual rank lies in the faithful execution of divine commands as a prerequisite for higher degrees of excellence.
